chunks: A Name of God is other than Him, and everything upon which the name of a thing falls is a creature, apart from God. As for what tongues express or hands perform, it is a creation. And God is an end-point among His end-points, and the end-directed is other than the end-point, and the end-point is describable, and every describable thing is manufactured. The Maker of things is not described by a named limit; He did not come into being so that His coming-into-being would be known through the creation of another, and He did not terminate at an end-point except that it would be other than Him.

Whoever understands this principle will never slip, and it is the pure Tawhid — so observe it, affirm it, and comprehend it by the permission of God. Whoever claims to recognise God through a veil, or through an image, or through a resemblance, is a polytheist, because His veil, His resemblance, and His image are other than Him. He is One, uniquely One — so how can one declare His Oneness who claims to have recognised Him through something other than Him?

Indeed, only the one who recognises Him through God has recognised God. Whoever does not recognise Him through Him has not recognised Him; he has only recognised something other than Him. There is nothing between the Creator and the created, and God is the Creator of things — not from any thing that was. And God is named with His Names, yet He is other than His Names, and the Names are other than Him.

key_terms.الأسماء: The Names of God; distinct from the Essence itself
key_terms.التوحيد الخالص: Pure Tawhid — undiluted Divine Unity, free from any mediation or anthropomorphism
key_terms.الغاية: End-point or telos; used philosophically to mean any bounded terminus or describable attribute
key_terms.المخلوق: The created; everything that falls under a name is a creature
key_terms.المصنوع: The manufactured/made; everything describable is made
key_terms.كيْنُونِيَّة: Coming-into-being, mode of existence — God's being is not a coming-into-existence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq teach about God's Names and pure Tawhid in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), presents one of the most sophisticated formulations of apophatic theology in Shia Islam, addressing the transcendence of God's Names from His Essence. The Imam articulates that every name is other than the named — the act of naming places something in the category of created, bounded things — whereas God transcends all naming and delimitation. The teaching was directed to initiates in the doctrine of pure Tawhid, warning against any form of anthropomorphism or mediated knowledge of God, which the Imam classifies as shirk (associating partners with God). The historical context is the early Abbasid period, when speculative theology (kalam) was flourishing and various schools debated the nature of God's attributes — the Imam's teaching directly refutes those who would know God through veils, images, or analogies.
word_analysis: and the one with an end-point
so that it would be known

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from one of his companions, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Ali Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid Bin Yazeed, from Abdul A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is other than Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and everything upon which a name occurs, is a thing, so it would be a creature, apart from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. 
So, as for what the tongues express, or the hands perform, so it is a creation, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is an end-point from His<sup>azwj</sup> (Created) end-points, and the end-point without the ending; and the end-point is an attribute, and every attribute is a creation, and the Creator of the things is other than the attribute by the limitation of the named. He<sup>azwj</sup> did not come into being so His<sup>azwj</sup> coming into being would be recognised by the creation of someone else, and one would not end up to an end-point except that it would be other than Him<sup>azwj</sup>.

Do not stumble from understanding this rule, and it is the pure Tawheed (Oneness). Therefore, recognise it, and ratify it, and understand it by the Permission of Allahazwj. The one who claims that he recognises Allahazwj by veils, or by an image, or by a resemblance, so he is a Polytheists, because Hisazwj veil, and Hisazwj resemblance, and Hisazwj image, is other than Himazwj, and rather Heazwj is One, with Oneness. So how can one consider Himazwj as Oneazwj, the one who claims that he is recognising Himazwj with something else?.

And rather, he has recognised Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the one who recognises him by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So the one who does not recognise Him<sup>azwj</sup> by Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so he has not recognised Him<sup>azwj</sup>, but he has recognised other than Him<sup>azwj</sup>. There isn’t between the Creator and the Created, a thing, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Creator of the things, not from a thing which was (beforehand). And Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Named with His<sup>azwj</sup> Names, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is other than His<sup>azwj</sup> Names, and the Names are other than Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah has narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from some of his people from Bakr ibn Salih from Ali ibn Salih from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Yazid from ‘Abd al-A‘la from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), who has said the following. “The name of Allah is something other than Allah Himself. Every thing that is called a thing is created except Allah. Whatever is expressed by the tongue or is worked out by hands are all created. The word Allah is one example of names and an end for naming. The end is different from the thing for which it is. The end is describable is created. The Maker of things is not describable by the limits of the fact behind the name. He did not become, so His becoming a being would have been recognized through the making of what is other than Him. He did not end up where there was another’s end.

Do not ever move away from understanding this rule. This is the true and pure believe in the Oneness of Allah. Observe it, acknowledge it and understand it by the permission of Allah. Those who think they understand Allah by means of covering, form or examples they become polytheists because his covering, form and example are not Him. He is only One and One alone. How can one form a belief in His Oneness by thinking that one may know Him through things other than Him.

One comes to know Allah only by Allah His Own self. One who can not know Him by His Own self he has not known Him. He only comes to know some thing else. There is nothing between the Creator and the created. All is the Creator of things but not from a thing that was there already. Allah’s names are His names but He is different from His Own names and the names are other than Him.”
